name: Agent attack gallery
description: Ten named attacks, including MCP authorization attacks, each run ungoverned and governed against an in-process mock stack: see what the attacker gets, then the control that refuses it.

name: Agent Audit Trail LAB
description: Who did what through which agent: seeded synthetic events from six sources, a read-only audit tool surface, and a correlation join into one timeline per action, with a tamper-evident hash chain. Fully mock; Live is refused.

name: Agent Gateway Inspector LAB
description: Inspector for an AI/agent gateway (PingOne Privilege) that allows, denies or holds agent tool calls for a human, with a decision buffer and a verifiable audit trail. Driven by an in-process stub gateway; nothing real is touched. Mock only: Live is refused.

name: Agent Governance LAB
description: AI Platform Agents: cross-cloud inventory of 13 sources, a five-level permission review, custodian approval before any action, remediation, a safe sync that never mistakes silence for deletion, AgentCore gateway governance and private-network discovery. Mock or Live. All product claims UNVERIFIED.

name: Agent Meets the MCP Door LAB
description: A member's own AI agent reaches an enterprise MCP door: discover, register, consent, per-call token exchange, gateway, policy decision, human approval, audit. Movable React Flow sequence diagram with a payload or mock token under each message, talk track and presenter mode. Mock only.

name: Agent Privilege Client LAB
description: A local, no-login test client for an OAuth-protected MCP gateway. Shows one tool call through the gateway and directly, so the policy difference is visible.

name: Agent Privilege Field Guide
description: The five sections of the PingOne Privilege Agent Privilege console area as a guided tour: Agent Registry, Agentic Apps, Federated Identity, Self-Hosted Agents, AI Platform Agents, plus the Identity/Grant/Guardrail mental model. From the field guide; deck-only behaviours labelled UNVERIFIED.

name: Agent Privilege K8 Kits
description: Download hub for the Agent Privilege Gateway Kubernetes deployment kits: the single-gateway quick-start package and the multi-gateway HA package (shared Redis, integrated load balancer), plus the shared 18-page deployment guide served inline. Read-only artifact server, offline.

name: Agent Registry Lifecycle
description: Register an AI agent as a non-human identity, grant it to a tool, rotate it by replacement, retire it, and watch the gateway refuse it (401/403/429). Mock only. Optional owner-run live checks compare with a real Privilege console.

name: Aggregate entitlement lab
description: See how an MCP aggregate lists only the tools each caller may use and refuses the rest by name: six checks, guided steps and a diagram. Mock simulates the Ping release claim (UNVERIFIED on our tenant); Real measures your own gateway's aggregate apps with your agent keys.

name: AI Intents Console Lab
description: The Privilege console's AI Intents page as a standalone: define intents with exemplars, twins, floors and Acts, point an app at them, and resolve agent actions through an encoder sidecar. Shapes measured from the console swagger; the resolution engine is lab-invented and labelled.

name: AI Policies LAB
description: Scope and HITL: four layered scope checks (surface, application, action, end user) on a real RS256 token you mint locally, a call held for a person, single-use approvals bound to the exact call, fail closed. Simulates release claims, all UNVERIFIED. Mock tables or a Live local engine.

name: Cedar act.sub Lab
description: Does Privilege's Cedar match the agent's act.sub claim? Measured once on a real tenant (2026-11-16, one real agent), simulated here: same token, two tools, one act.sub policy each. The matching one is allowed, the one naming a different agent is refused. Mock only; Real is owner-run.

name: Cedar in Privilege Lab
description: A guided tour of Cedar AI policies in PingOne Privilege: hold a call for a human, narrow a token's scope, and match the agent's act.sub claim. Set-up guide and a Cedar IS / IS NOT panel. Simulated here; only the act.sub case was measured on a real tenant (one agent, one run).

name: Coding Agents LAB
description: Inspection inside Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot and Antigravity: hooks as the enforcement point, the outcome follows the risk. Opens in Real mode — every decision is the live Privilege AI Guard on our tenant; Mock and Live are the offline rehearsal.

name: Data Protection LAB
description: AIGuard content inspection in and out with graduated outcomes, your own gitleaks rules, personal-data kinds with checksums, Agent Insights, the OWASP Agentic Top 10, and sealed prompt logging. Mock reads tables; Live runs locally; a Privilege check sends the text through the live AI Guard.

name: Federated Identity LAB
description: Simulates the 2026-11-02 Ping release claims for Federated Identity (short-lived tokens, issuer, subject and audience binding, lifetimes, key refresh, revocation) and Self-Hosted Agents, with real local RS256 verification. Mock tables or a Live local engine. Every product claim is UNVERIFIED.

name: Gateway Claims Lab
description: What gateway v1.261024 added, in mock: a nested-claim gate (client_id + act.sub via RequiredClaims, including the act-as-text trap) and an AgentCore gateway posture view (shape only, values invented), plus two H2 2026 release tabs (on-behalf-of RFC 8693 exchange, AgentCore gateway governance...

name: Hostile A2A / poisoned Agent Card
description: A deliberately hostile A2A agent, an offline delegating generalist, and a pinned-card client shown side by side with an ungoverned one: the card told my agent to include my token.

name: Hostile MCP / rug-pull
description: A deliberately hostile MCP server, an offline victim, and a pinned client shown side by side with an ungoverned one: the tool that changed overnight.

name: Intent, Purpose and Behaviour Lab
description: Three signals asked of every call (intent, purpose, behaviour), plus on-behalf-of and ID-JAG flows, modelling the 2026-11-02 Ping release claims. Mock reads tables; Live signs for real (RS256) locally; a Privilege check sends the call through the live AI Guard on our tenant.

name: MCP Demo Client for Privilege LAB
description: Chat-first local MCP demo client for protected MCP demos behind a PingOne Privilege gateway.

name: MCP Elicitation LAB
description: An MCP server mid-tool-call asks the person for more: form mode and URL mode, accept / decline / cancel, -32042, and the spec's safety rules, with findings when a server breaks them. Mock server and mock client; nothing is fetched.

name: MCP inspector
description: Connect to an MCP server, list its tools, resources and prompts, scan them, then call tools behind a confirm step. One app with the scanner (D4).

name: MCP scanner
description: Scan the metadata an MCP server serves, or a pasted tools/list snapshot, for tool poisoning before an agent reads it. Reports; never blocks. Same app as the inspector (D3).

name: MCP Surface LAB
description: The MCP gateway in front of every MCP server: aggregate policy caps, entitlement-aware discovery, OpenAPI to MCP, five backend credential modes, a verified-server catalog, OAuth 2.1 with PKCE and CIMD, approval-gated creation. Simulates the 2026-11-02 release claims. Mock or Live. UNVERIFIED.

name: Meridian Pay A2A hop lab
description: Walk a delegated agent token chain one hop at a time: sign in, hand the job to a platform-signed external agent, exchange tokens (RFC 8693, third-party subject and actor), and call MCP tools through Privilege doors. Every hop shows sub/act/aud/scope, and refusals are demoed on purpose. Runs…

name: Muse
description: A personal agent (Muse) calls tools through a PingOne Privilege-shaped gateway, with a DaVinci-shaped detection flow in front. Simulated: no tenant, no OBO.

name: PF → Privilege OBO Lab
description: Simulated PingFederate to Privilege OBO chain: user SSO, RFC 8693 exchange (sub=user, act.sub=agent), federated-identity check, grant tiers, Cedar policy, Pass Agent Token passthrough. Interactive flow walk, eight scenarios, refusals mirror measured log lines, twelve-card issues panel. Mock only.

name: Ping Services Stub LAB
description: One stub exercising every shared Ping service the family deploys: shared local PingFederate, PingGateway, Privilege Agent Gateway, PingOne (SaaS), PingOne Privilege console, and the SE-K8s PingFederate. One real, read-only call per service; Mock/Real toggle; reuses shared infra (shared-first rule).

name: Privilege A2A Anthropic demo LAB
description: Three Node processes that show an access review through A2A and MCP, on Anthropic or Google models.

name: Privilege API Explorer LAB
description: Sign in to a PingOne Privilege console with a user API key and secret, then browse all 447 console API operations from the swagger catalog with substring search and filters, and run each one live with real-time status, timing and response. Mock by default; Real is owner-run.

name: Privilege Bulk Users LAB
description: Register users for PingOne Privilege by API, in bulk: a guide to the two routes (PingOne API, Privilege console API) and a runnable lab with plan, typed-count apply and verify, 429 back-off, and six Mock scenarios. Mock by default; Real is owner-run.

name: Privilege demo LAB
description: An AI agent's MCP tool calls pass a policy enforcement point that decides allow, deny or hold with Cedar. Runs offline in mock mode (in-process mock issuer and tool backends) or verifies Bearer tokens from your own PingFederate in live mode.

name: Privilege Google Secrets Lab
description: Privilege Hubs brokering a Google Secret Manager credential to an AI agent: the agent holds only a Privilege agent key; the gateway policy allows the in-scope secret (custodian release) and refuses the out-of-scope ask. Mock gateway, custodian and secret manager; mock-issued secret labelled.

name: Privilege Logging Lab
description: Drive each Privilege gateway use case and see what gets logged, scored on user, agent, tool and policy decision. Mock replays 17 transactions measured on 2026-11-07; Real (owner-run) sends them to your gateway and reads the log back. The gaps are listed, not hidden.

name: Privilege Map LAB
description: The PingOne Privilege Federated Identity model as ReactFlow diagrams you can drag and walk through, plus 21 Privilege feature cards, stories and a talk track. Mock only.

name: Privilege OWASP Lab
description: The OWASP Agentic AI Top 10 (ASI01-ASI10) with PingOne Privilege coverage: the slide-21 table from the Capability Overview deck, ten explained category cards, and the Gateway vs AIGuard split. The two stated gaps are labelled, not hidden. Mock is static deck wording offline; Real adds read-only live

name: SaaS Access LAB
description: Just-in-time, time-bound access to six platforms (GitHub, GitLab, Salesforce, Snowflake, Databricks, Google Workspace): approval chains, blocked self-approval, expiry, receipts, drift. Mock is read-only; Live runs real local state; a Privilege check sends the request through the live AI Guard.

name: Secrets Vault LAB
description: A per-user credential vault (self-service, no administrator override, real AES-256-GCM, injected by a simulated gateway) and secret store management over five mock providers (AWS, GCP, Azure, Delinea, CyberArk). Mock or Live mode. Every product claim is UNVERIFIED on our tenant.
